WORKFORCE / TRIBAL NATIONS

Staff and community
housing on tribal land.

For tribal governments, housing authorities and tribal enterprises.

Private rooms with their own bath for clinic, school and enterprise staff, and for people waiting on a permanent home.

Start a conversationSee the units

THE PROBLEM

Too few homes for families, and nowhere for new staff.

Clinics, schools and enterprises recruit staff who have nowhere to live, while families wait for homes. A room for a new nurse or teacher keeps a needed role filled, and transitional rooms help while permanent homes are built.

HOW TRIBES USE IT

One unit family, many community needs.

Staff
Clinic, school and enterprise staff, including travel nurses and new teachers.
Transition
Transitional rooms while permanent homes are built.
Elders
Accessible units with a ramp to the door and a roll-in bath pod.
Land
Placed on tribal land under tribal approvals. Ground screws suit remote, uneven sites.
Owner
Owned by the tribe or its housing authority, and leased to staff or residents.

PAYING FOR IT

Ways tribes fund it.

  • Grants

    Federal housing grants

    Formula and competitive federal grants for tribes and tribal housing entities.

  • Services

    School and clinic budgets

    Staff housing paid for by the school or clinic it serves.

  • Enterprise

    Tribal enterprise

    Staff housing for casinos, resorts and enterprises, funded by the enterprise.

Eligibility and rules are set by each program. We check fit on the first call. Outpost units are private rooms for one or two people, not family homes.

THE UNITS

One shell family.
Built for crews and staff.

Every market on this page uses Outpost: private rooms with a factory-built bath pod and a kitchenette, on the same 4 ft wall module. Mix the layouts in one cluster.
